candidates.label: Sea of Galilee
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate is corroborated by OpenBible.info's independently recorded point for the same lake.

summary.text: The Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake in the Jordan Rift Valley, more than 200 meters below sea level, fed principally by the Jordan River, which enters from the north and exits to the south. The Jewish historian Josephus gives its size as forty furlongs wide and one hundred forty furlongs long (roughly 7 by 26 km) and describes its water as sweet, pure and good to drink. Several towns stood on its shores in the first century, among them Capernaum on the northwest shore and Tiberias, a city that Herod Antipas built on the lake and named after the emperor Tiberius.

history.text: The lake's western shore lay in Galilee, but Josephus gives Galilee's eastern border as the territories of Hippos and Gadara and Gaulanitis, and he places both Bethsaida, near where the Jordan enters the lake, and Gamala, on the eastern side, in Gaulanitis. This project places the lake in Galilee, after which the New Testament names it the "sea of Galilee."

The Gospels set much of Jesus' Galilean ministry around the lake. He called his first disciples, the fishermen Simon and Andrew, as they cast a net into it; on its water he "rebuked the wind and the sea," and on another night he came to his disciples "walking on the sea." John, who also calls the lake "the Sea of Tiberias," describes Jesus appearing to his disciples there after his resurrection.
Today the lake, known in Hebrew as Lake Kinneret, lies in northern Israel. Capernaum's excavated site and other places around the shore draw Christian pilgrims and tourists.

scripture.textWEB: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
He entered into a boat and crossed over, and came into his own city.
In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
Jesus departed from there and came near to the sea of Galilee; and he went up on the mountain and sat there.
Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
After these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.

otConnections.note: The lake is called the 'Sea of Chinnereth' in the Old Testament, an older name for the same body of water later known as the Sea of Galilee or Sea of Tiberias.
